audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and whys[5] are swapped against their rows, and the level-6 comparison itself is backwards — the page says Shen's global 'cancels the one tool that gave you an edge'.
audit.why: The whys array maps to Level 1 / Level 2 / Level 3 / Levels 4-5 / Level 6 / First item / Two+ items. whys[4] (the Level 6 row) reads 'First item stays even', and whys[5] (the First item row) is the Hero's Entrance versus Stand United comparison. On the substance: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s and lands with a knockup, a taunt and an ally shield; Stand United is 200/180/160s and only shields plus teleports. Galio's global is 20 seconds shorter at every rank and it is the one that wins a fight on arrival.
audit.corrected: Rows unswapped, and level 6 now reads as Galio's spike with the two cooldowns compared.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (a) Spirit's Refuge is described as if it blanks Galio generally — it blocks attacks only. (b) Twilight Assault's max-health scaling and its collision requirement are never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot on Spirit's Refuge: 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked.' Attacks, not abilities — Winds of War, the Shield of Durand taunt and Justice Punch all land straight through it, which turns a supposedly dead window into a poke window. Riot on Twilight Assault: 'Shen recalls his spirit blade to attack with it, dealing damage based on the target's max health. The attacks are greatly empowered if it collides with an enemy champion, and all collided enemies are slowed while running away from Shen.' Max-health scaling punishes exactly the HP a Galio buys, the empowerment needs the blade to pass through you, and the slow only applies while you run AWAY from him.
audit.corrected: Poke through the Refuge with abilities and never autos; stand off the blade's line; do not run directly away after being collided.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Shadow Dash with no numbers and no cost.
audit.why: Shadow Dash 18/16/14/12/10s for 150 energy — that cost matters, because Shen runs on energy and cannot chain it with Twilight Assault (140/130/120/110/100) and Spirit's Refuge (40). Spirit's Refuge is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. Against Justice Punch at 11/10/9/8/7s, an early Shadow Dash spend leaves a 7-second gap where you have a punch and he has nothing.
audit.corrected: Numbers and the energy cost written into the cooldown block, winCon, phases[2] and loading.

audit.why: Shen has no heal — Ki Barrier is a shield, and shields are not reduced by Grievous Wounds. The line sends the player to buy the wrong item.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the Spirit's Refuge cue.

edits.before: Level 1 leans Shen: he takes Q (Twilight Assault) and pulls his spirit blade through you for empowered autos while you only have Winds of War and no engage, so don't step up — farm with the tornado's center column and poke him from max range instead. At 3 with Q-W-E you get your first real window: don't walk blindly into a trade, start the Shield of Durand channel as he steps in so the magic-amp damage reduction sponges his empowered autos, release the taunt, then Justice Punch out. Watch his W (Spirit's Refuge): while it's up it blocks your Colossal Smash empowered autos, so commit your trades when it's on cooldown, not into it.
edits.after: Level 1 leans Shen: he takes Q (Twilight Assault) and pulls his spirit blade through you for empowered autos that scale off your max health, while you only have Winds of War and no engage — so don't step up, farm with the tornado and poke from max range. The blade only gets that empowerment if it collides with you, so stand off its line. At 3 with Q-W-E you get your first real window: start the Shield of Durand charge as he steps in so the magic-amp reduction sponges his blade autos, release the taunt, then Justice Punch out. And note what Spirit's Refuge blocks — attacks, not abilities, so the tornado still lands through it.

edits.before: From 4 to 6 this is a poke-and-stalemate lane: your Q tornado out-ranges his short spirit-blade trades, but he sits behind Spirit's Refuge and sustains, and neither of you kills the other through full shields. Six is your one true swing — Hero's Entrance means you don't have to win this lane at all. When Shen presses Stand United to save a dying ally, you can flag onto the same fight, drop on his carry's killer, or punish whatever lane he abandoned. Treat the 1v1 as a tie and let your global decide the game, because in lane he just farms and waits you out.
edits.after: From 4 to 6 this is a poke-and-stalemate lane: your Q tornado out-ranges his 400-range blade trades, and Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks rather than abilities, so keep poking through it and simply don't auto into it. Six is your one true swing — Hero's Entrance is 180 seconds against Stand United's 200, and yours arrives with a knockup and a taunt while his only shields. When Shen presses R to save a dying ally, flag onto the same fight or punish whatever lane he abandoned. Treat the 1v1 as a tie and let your global decide the game.

edits.before: Late game tilts back to Shen. Both of you flatten into utility tanks who do no real damage in a duel, but his kit out-teamfights yours: Stand United shields a carry from across the map and his Q taunt-cleave hits a cluster, while your value is a single-target Justice Punch knockup plus the same Hero's Entrance roam he also has. Don't try to 1v1 him for the splitpush — he trades evenly and his Spirit's Refuge blocks your autos indefinitely. Win through teamfight timing and using your knockup to set up your team, not by trying to out-stat him one-on-one.
edits.after: Late game tilts back to Shen. Both of you flatten into utility tanks who do no real damage in a duel, but Twilight Assault hits off your max health — exactly the stat you keep buying — and Ki Barrier shields him every time he casts anything. Don't try to 1v1 him for the splitpush; he trades evenly and Spirit's Refuge blocks your autos on a 10-second cooldown late. Your edge is that your global is 20 seconds shorter and lands as CC rather than a shield: win on teamfight timing and use the knockup to set up your team.

notes: The whys array had Level 6 and First item swapped (whys[4] read 'First item stays even', whys[5] carried the level-6 global comparison) — worth checking whether that off-by-one hit other Galio matchups generated in the same batch. The global comparison was also factually backwards: the page said Shen's Stand United 'cancels' Galio's edge, when Hero's Entrance is 20 seconds shorter at every rank and arrives as a knockup, taunt and shield rather than a shield alone. Left alone as UNVERIFIED: whether Spirit's Refuge blocks the Colossal Smash on-hit component specifically (Riot says 'attacks' are blocked and Colossal Smash is an empowered attack, so I wrote the attack-level claim only), and whether Shen's Shadow Dash taunt can be cleansed or shortened by tenacity — the kit's needsResearch is empty, which means unknown, not no. content.win[1], win[2], win[5], win[6] read 'Shen' (4) and cannot be changed to 'Galio' (5) or 'Skill' (5) inside the length band if the user later wants the chart adjusted.
